crop: Cocoa (Theobroma cacao), improved hybrids (IRAD, SODECAO), Centre and South Cameroon

bearing.text: First yields 18 months after planting improved seedlings, a full crop after two and a half to three years; second generation IRAD varieties average two tonnes per ha against one for the first generation (S1, 2020). SNK hybrids enter production from 30 months (S2, 2026). First production usually at 3 to 4 years, significant at 5 to 7 (S3, 2026).

density.text: 850 to 1,100 plants per ha depending on topography and agroforestry system; shade 70% up to 15 years (S4, 2025). 1,100 to 1,300 plants per ha (S3). 1,333 at 3 m x 2.5 m (S2). Pilot plots: 972 cocoa with 1,180 plantain as temporary shade per ha (S5).

plants.text: Seedlings 150 to 250 FCFA each (S2). Shade trees 50,000 to 200,000 FCFA per ha (S3).

fertilizer.text: NPK 12-11-18 + 3 MgO, 300 to 400 g per tree a year from year 4 in 2 to 3 splits; every 3 years 5 t/ha of manure or compost (S2).

protection.text: Black pod (Phytophthora megakarya) reached 34 to 71% of pods on untreated trees against under 2% with Ridomil (S6). Copper or metalaxyl copper every 3 weeks in the risk period, June to October; insecticide against mirids in two passes 21 days apart; 4 to 6 treatments a year (S2). No treatment in the 14 days before harvest (S4).

post_harvest.text: Pod opening within 5 days, fermentation 6 days with 3 turnings, sun drying 8 to 15 days to 6 to 8% moisture (S4).

yields.text: Small unaided farms 280 kg/ha, supported farms 500 to 600 kg/ha (S7). Poorly kept 300 to 500 kg, well managed 800 to 1,500 kg per ha (S3). Projection 250, 700 and 1,200 kg/ha in years 3, 4 and 5, then 1,800 (S2).

prices.text: ONCC minimum buying price 1,400 FCFA/kg on 21 April 2026, up from 1,050 in January; 900 FCFA/kg in some zones early 2026 (S8). Farm gate 1,650 to 1,700 FCFA/kg on 8 June 2026; never above 2,000 FCFA in the 2025 to 2026 season (S9). 1,600 FCFA/kg at the start of the 2023 campaign, which opens in September with large harvests from late October (S10).
